Lozenge capacity of 2 billion annualized already in place with packaging bottlenecks resolved; only maintenance capex needed for…
Injectable/IV products capacity being expanded from ~54 lakh units per month to 75-78 lakh units per month, plus new…

deepdive.sec: Pharma / Branded Generics & CDMO Integration Play

bull_bear.body: Final dividend INR 9.3/share recommended for FY26; Net cash position of INR 1,200cr available for integration needs or debt reduction post-merger.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: CDMO execution delays persisting beyond Q1; West Asia geopolitical tensions affecting international shipments; higher-than-expected field force attrition during integration; merger approval delays (hearing scheduled mid-June).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Candid on short-term pain ('operational reset'), confident on long-term branded growth trajectory, cautious on near-term CDMO timing but bullish on customer pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 5% revenue de-growth is entirely artificial due to strategic exit of trade generics; underlying branded engine is accelerating (8% vs 2% reported). CDMO stagnation is purely an internal resource bottleneck (lean dev team) despite having top-tier global clients.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: India Business: INR 526cr (+2% YoY), Branded only +8%; FY26 India INR 2,461cr (+9%), Branded +11%. International Formulations: INR 259cr (-9% YoY) due to shipping constraints. CDMO: INR 110cr approx (-22% YoY), FY26 flat at INR 445cr.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Execution delays in CDMO despite strong order book | Divi's Laboratories | beneficiary | Med | If JB/Customer outsource excess demand due to internal bottlenecks, pure-play CDMOs may see spillover. |

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin improved to 70% (+400bps YoY) driven by discontinuation of low-margin trade generics (previously 7-8% of India sales) and better product mix. Procurement and corporate overhead synergies visible from April.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: India branded business to return to low-teens growth in 2-3 quarters; International single-digit growth from Q2FY27; CDMO to turn positive on 12-month basis pending execution fix; Gross margin base set at ~70% but full-year guidance withheld pending Q1 trend.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: CDMO has sufficient new projects/contracts with top 5 OTC players; growth constrained by execution delays not demand.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Chronic therapy expansion (cardiac) leveraging Torrent's wider distribution; CDMO wallet share increase with existing giants (Innova, Kenvue, P&G); geographic expansion of current products within existing customer bases.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: JB Pharma underwent a deliberate operational reset in Q4FY26 post-Torrent acquisition, causing a 5% revenue dip and one-off charges, but underlying branded India business grew 8% with gross margins expanding 400bps to 70% due to low-margin trade generic exit. Normalization to double-digit growth is expected from Q2FY27 as integration synergies (procurement, distribution) kick in and CDMO execution delays are resolved.

open.item: Slight pricing pressure flagged on 2 key US molecules, expected to be neutralized over the remaining part of the year with good order visibility for next 4-6 months.
Operating cash flow to operating EBITDA expected in the range of 75% to 78% for full year FY26.
Treasury/other income expected in the range of INR65 to INR70 crore next year (FY26) given the growing net cash surplus.
Filing around 8 to 10 progressive products every year from FY27 across ~40 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, Southeast Asia and Middle East to drive BGX demand and pricing.
Gross margin improved ~4% to around 70% (from 66%) on trade generics reset and product mix; full-year gross margin guidance deferred pending one more quarter (Q1 to be indicative).

Q4 FY26 (first quarter post Torrent change of control on 21 Jan 2026) described as an operational reset that temporarily impacted performance, with normalization expected beginning Q1 FY27 and continuing forward.

JB-Torrent merger in last stage with requisite shareholder approvals received; NCLT hearing scheduled second week of June 2026 and merger expected to become effective within one to two months maximum.
JB India field force at ~2,500 MRs with no change yet; expected to reduce a little going ahead as brands/divisions merge, with an update at the end of the coming quarter.
Ophthalmology portfolio expected to reach a consistent INR17 crore to INR18 crore per month run-rate in the next 3 to 4 months, with double-digit growth.
Ophthalmology business (currently 6th ranked, growing 19%) aspires to be a top-5 company within 9 months to a year.
India business expected to recover to double-digit / low-teens growth trajectory over maybe a couple of quarters.
International business single-digit growth expected to resume potentially from Q1 but more likely from Q2 FY27, with West Asia container constraints uncertain in Q1.

Container shipment constraints (primarily West Asia, also Asia/Southeast Asia) flagged as an international headwind; Asia expected to catch up in Q1 but West Asia uncertain, with on-track expected Q2 onwards.

Integration synergies targeted from procurement, corporate overhead/back-end overlapping functions and distribution network optimization (effective from April), plus revenue synergies from brand complementarity expected to start in the next couple of quarters.
Ophthalmology perpetual license triggers in December 2026, making JB full custodian of trademarks and lifting gross margin from ~20% towards domestic (~66%) profile, significantly EBITDA-accretive.
USD116 million payment due before December 2026 intended to be paid entirely from internal accruals.
US business expected to grow from USD30 million to USD50 million in a couple of years (two to three years).

Trade generics business (about 7-8% of India top line till Q3) discontinued/significantly rationalized; not a focus and no reinvestment planned, keeping reported India growth below branded growth until it laps out of the base in Q4 FY27.
CDMO business (down 22% in Q4 on high base, flat at INR445 crore for FY26) expected to have positive momentum on a 12-month basis in FY27, as flat is not normal for the business.

ROW export pipeline: first phase of 8 to 10 molecules across 14 to 16 key markets to get approvals from September/October 2025, launch quantities from Q4FY26, full annualized benefit from FY27; further phases over next 2-3 years.

verdicts.item: All big brands expected to only get bigger driven by volume growth, particularly strong performance in the chronic space (Cilacar +25%, Cilacar-T +33%, Nicardia +30%, Sporlac +13%).
verdicts.note: 'The chronic business grew at 19% versus the industry growth of 14%' — big chronic brands continued outperforming.

verdicts.item: CDMO quarterly run-rate targeted to step up from ~INR110 crore to ~INR150 crore per quarter starting next financial year (FY27) as marquee projects commercialize.
verdicts.note: CDMO Q4 -22%, FY26 flat; FY27 run-rate 'premature to give' with execution challenges — the ~150cr/qtr target deferred/uncertain.

verdicts.item: Overall gross margins expected to be closer to 65% for the coming 2 years.
verdicts.note: 'Gross margin improved to around 70%' — FY26 GM ~68-69%, well above ~65%.

verdicts.item: Torrent Pharma to acquire KKR's 46.39% controlling stake for INR11,917 crore cash triggering a mandatory open offer at INR1,639.18/share, followed by a merger with Torrent as surviving listed entity, subject to CCI and other approvals.
verdicts.note: 'Torrent Pharma acquired a controlling stake in JB Chemicals and Pharma on 21st January 2026'; shareholder approvals received, merger in last stage. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Azmarda run-rate of 125,000-130,000 units/month maintained, targeting 140,000+ units/month by end of H1 (next quarter).
verdicts.note: expired: no update 2Q past horizon Q2FY26

verdicts.item: India business expected to sustain growth three to four percentage points higher than the IPM market growth.
verdicts.note: 'India business grew at 11% versus the IPM growth of 10%' — only ~100 bps, below 3-4ppt. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Branded generic export (BGX) business expected at ~10% growth in FY26, improving to 12%+ (mid-teens) from FY27 as new progressive products commercialize.
verdicts.note: 'international formulations revenue grew 2% year-on-year to INR1,154 crores' in FY26 — below the ~10% BGX guide.

verdicts.item: Four to five big CDMO projects (lozenges for Europe/US, Pan-India ORS, throat spray for cough & cold, iodine-based syrup/ointment) to be commercialized by end of the year / next 12-18 months.
verdicts.note: 'JB has some delays in execution of these contracts... accelerate the delivery of these new products' — CDMO project commercialization delayed.

verdicts.item: CDMO business expected to grow between 12% and 14% in the coming period as partner inventory has normalized.
verdicts.note: 'CDMO... For the year, it was flat at INR445 crores' — below 12-14%.

verdicts.item: Full-year gross margin guidance held at around 67%.
verdicts.note: 'Gross margin improved to around 70% from 66%' — FY26 GM ~68-69%, above the ~67% guide.

verdicts.item: ESOP cost guided at INR41-46 crore in FY26 and INR26 crore in FY27; total ~INR75 crore remaining to be charged over next two to two-and-half years.
verdicts.note: Change of control accelerated remaining ESOP: 'one-offs including non-cash ESOP charges amounted to INR40 crores' in Q4 alone — FY26 ESOP above the 41-46cr guide. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Gross margin expected to improve around 30 to 50 basis points in FY26 supported by cost initiatives and mix.
verdicts.note: FY26 GM ~68-69% vs FY25 66.4% — well above the +30-50bps guide.
